name: Leydig Cell Hypoplasia due to Luteinizing Hormone Beta (LHB) Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Leydig Cell Hypoplasia due to LHB Deficiency

criteria.description: Presence of undervirilization or ambiguous genitalia in 46,XY individuals
Low or undetectable serum luteinizing hormone (LH) with low testosterone and elevated follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the LHB gene
Testicular biopsy showing Leydig cell hypoplasia or absence

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical features consistent with Leydig cell hypoplasia, characteristic hormonal profile, and confirmation by genetic testing of LHB mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other causes of hypogonadism and disorders of sexual development.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes micropenis, hypospadias, or female external genitalia
searchTerms: unclear male genitalia in XY individuals
ambiguous genital appearance in genetic males
uncertain external genitalia in genetic males

pathognomonic.symptomName: Undervirilization with absent or sparse pubic hair
searchTerms: sparse or absent pubic hair in males

pathognomonic.notes: Undescended testes common in affected males

common.notes: Failure to develop secondary sexual characteristics
Breast tissue development due to hormonal imbalance
Due to impaired Leydig cell function and testosterone deficiency

occasional.symptomName: Osteopenia or decreased bone mineral density

occasional.notes: Non-specific symptom associated with hormonal deficiency
searchTerms: tiredness due to low male hormones
low energy related to hormone deficiency

occasional.symptomName: Mild gynecological features such as vaginal bleeding in rare cases

rare.notes: May be secondary to chronic hormonal imbalance

searchTerms: symptoms like high blood pressure and obesity

laboratory: Low or undetectable serum LH levels
imaging: Ultrasound showing small or undescended testes
MRI pelvis may show hypoplastic Leydig cells
other: Histopathology of testicular biopsy showing Leydig cell hypoplasia

distinguishingFeatures: Female external genitalia with 46,XY karyotype but normal testosterone levels
Normal or elevated LH and testosterone levels
Impaired conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone

redFlags: Ambiguous genitalia in a newborn male
Failure to undergo puberty by age 14 in males
